title: an-instrument-that-cannot-bite-is-refused-at-the-verdict
intention: A criterion's verdict carries evidence that its instrument COULD have said no — the observation of that same instrument aimed at a tree which does not carry the fix — so a criterion cannot pass by naming a measure that was never capable of failing.
why: MEASURED n=3 in a single voyage (staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk, 2026-08-17): three of eight acceptance criteria named an instrument that could not have shown what the criterion claimed. C2 said 'grep staleness.py for mtime, ImportError, __cached__' and expected zero — 16 hits came back, every one from the module's own explanatory prose and the deliberately retained retired comparison, so the instrument was incapable of distinguishing a fixed predicate from an unfixed one. C4 said 'revert the predicate and watch test_discovery.py go red' — it stays green, because the prove-apart pair injects the staleness answer, so the revert cannot red no matter what the predicate does. C7's grep counted the correction's own verbatim quotation of the sentence it corrects. All three read as reasonable when written; all three would have passed any text predicate over the instrument string. The chain has no stage at which a criterion's instrument is executed at a moment when it could fail: validate authors it before the code exists (that is the whole point of the stage), and the verdict runs it exactly once, afterwards, against a tree that carries the fix. One reading of one tree cannot separate 'this instrument agrees the build worked' from 'this instrument agrees with everything', and the second is a hollow green — which Law 8 rates worse than a red, because a red is distrusted by construction and a false green gets leaned on by a peer.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass; the exit gate's verdict is exactly that proof for the chart's criteria, and an instrument that cannot bite is the hollow one. Also Law 9 read onto the acceptance criterion itself: red is the default and green is earned, so an instrument already green before the build has earned nothing. And Law 3, in its operational form — the observation of the second tree IS the measurement; without it the criterion's outcome is a hypothesis wearing a verdict's clothes.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant, transcribed: PROVED + feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs proofs beside cairn/devices/builder/machines/verdict/ under isolation=netns, with teeth that refire this voyage's three falsified criteria carrying their ORIGINAL evidence and assert the door refuses each by name, and assert the three replacements that were actually run pass. The hollow-build trap has a name here: a tooth that only checks the field is PRESENT would go green against a door that accepts any string, so at least one tooth must red against HEAD's verdict_error. FEEDBACK-TO-ORIGIN: the origin is skills/chart's validate stage — a criterion refused at the verdict is a criterion validate should not have admitted — and the route back is orient's brick loop (deposit -> counsel -> propose), never a quiet edit of validate's judges. ENTRY GATE at BUILDME: chart claim + intent_berth + sorted_berth. EMISSION GATE on WATCHME: the probe below armed at its berth or WatchmeEmissionRed. CLEARANCE into PROVED: harbor_master.clearance.clear — and the builder device's charter must declare gated_by or that crossing refuses (measured 2026-08-17: 27 of 39 beside-code charters carry none).
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when the verdict door refuses an artifact whose criterion carries an instrument and evidence but no discriminating observation — proved by refiring this voyage's three falsified criteria with their original evidence and watching the refusal name each, while the three replacements that were actually run pass. WRONG INTENT if the field fills with sentences naming no second tree, no mutation and no revert: at that point the answer is a runnable instrument form, not a sterner sentence, and this ticket is the wrong SHAPE rather than an unfinished one.
falsifier.horizon: The next ten verdicts written through write_verdict after the field lands — read at the tenth, or 2026-09-17, whichever comes first.

children: none, because the split is one door predicate plus its proofs and they do not prove apart — verdict_error at cairn/devices/builder/machines/verdict/verdict.py already refuses a criterion lacking instrument or evidence with 'a verdict without both is narration', and this is that same refusal one clause longer. The escalation named in the falsifier (a runnable instrument form) is deliberately NOT a child: it is a different ticket, cast only if the watch says this one failed.

questions.a: TIME VERSUS CAPABILITY, AND THIS IS WHY THE TWO TICKETS DID NOT MERGE. a-validate-criterion-is-runnable-before-the-crossing (cast 2026-08-15, at TICKETME) holds the same field for a different failure: an instrument reading state that does not exist yet, so it cannot RUN when the exit gate demands its verdict. Its remedy is a text predicate over the instrument string at validate's door. This one's instrument runs, at the right moment, against real state, and cannot tell pass from fail. Neither fix reaches the other's defect: a text predicate cannot see a grep whose 16 hits are the module's own prose, and running an instrument earlier says nothing about whether it discriminates. Merging would give one ticket two falsifiers, which is how a ticket closes on the half that was cheap.

CAPABILITY IS NOT VISIBLE IN THE SENTENCE. This is the load-bearing observation and the reason the cheap fix was rejected. 'grep staleness.py for mtime and expect zero' is a well-formed, specific, falsifiable-looking instrument. Whether it can bite depends on what else in that file says the word — a fact about the TREE, not about the sentence. No predicate over instrument strings can ever answer it, which is why the ask is for an OBSERVATION rather than a better-worded criterion.

THE THREE REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, IN ORDER OF WHAT I WOULD BUILD IF THE FIELD WERE DIFFERENT. (a) Make `instrument` RUNNABLE and have validate's door execute it against the pre-build tree demanding RED — the cleanest expression of Law 9, and it changes what a criterion IS, because today instruments are prose ('read discovery.py's skip handling'). Bigger question, deliberately not opened. (b) A text predicate at validate's door — rejected by the distinction above. (c) Ask for the observation at the verdict — chosen: it cannot force the trip to the second tree, but it makes NOT taking it a thing that has to be written down, and it costs one clause in a door that already refuses two neighbouring absences.

THE HIDDEN ASSUMPTION IS NAMED AND WATCHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED AWAY. This rests on a builder who took no discriminating observation saying so instead of writing a plausible sentence — the same hollow-pass shape the /sorted door fights with its resolvable-referent rule, and I do not believe it holds unaided. The watch above is aimed at exactly that, with an early stop at n>=4 and a named escalation, so the assumption's failure is a measurement rather than a disappointment.

MUTATION-OF-THE-ARTIFACT-UNDER-TEST IS SETTLED PRACTICE HERE; AIMING IT AT THE CRITERION IS WHAT IS NEW. cairn/machines/build_inspector's proof mutates each seeded case in place and asserts the target tooth reds (6/6 killed), and this voyage's own replacement for C4 mutated loop.py's deciding branch at line 399. The technique is in-house and proven — the ticket borrows the pattern and cites it (charter `entry`), grafting no bytes.

HARD FOR NEW, SILENT FOR OLD — THE RETRO-RED DISPOSITION IS SETTLED AT CAST, NOT LEFT OPEN. 40+ berthed verdicts predate the field. The verdict door refuses a new artifact without it; the promotion judge says nothing about its absence. This is the same disposition a-piece-names-where-its-output-lands took at corpus 52 / carrying 1 / silent 51, and taking it here at cast is the lesson from that ticket applied rather than re-derived (Law 1).

THE COST IS REAL AND IT IS THE POINT. A discriminating observation means building a second tree. Measured price on the bearing voyage: three worktree round-trips inside 149 tool calls — and those three trips are precisely what caught the three hollow criteria. The cost bought the thing it cost for; at a worse ratio this ticket would be the wrong trade, and that ratio is unmeasured on any other voyage.

THIS DOES NOT CATCH THE DEFECT WHERE IT IS BORN, AND SAYS SO. validate authors the criterion before the code exists; a hollow one still gets written and still rides five stages before anything notices. The late catch is accepted deliberately, because the early catch requires the runnable instrument form named in the falsifier's WRONG INTENT clause.

watchme.nexus: the validate tree — the criterion is authored there, and what the tree needs to learn is which SHAPES of instrument turn out unable to bite
watchme.consumer: skills/chart's validate stage, and Akien at his gate if the early-stop fires
